editorial:
You know that feeling when a simple workday turns into a nightmare? Down drops you into an office elevator with two coworkers who think they are just stuck for a few hours. The setup is easy to follow, and the small space makes every conversation feel close and tense. At first, the pair shares snacks, stories, and a little chemistry, so you might expect a sweet holiday romance. Then the mood shifts, and you realize one of them has been hiding a darker side. The movie keeps things simple and direct, so you can focus on the characters instead of confusing plot twists.

The acting carries most of the weight, especially as fear and anger take over. The pacing starts slow, then builds into a nasty fight for survival. Some moments feel a little predictable, and the small setting can get repetitive, but the tension usually holds. If you like tight thrillers with one location, this is a solid pick. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray if you want the best picture. It is not perfect, but it gives you a quick, creepy ride.
endingExplained: Guy finally shows his true colors when he reveals he has been obsessed with Jennifer and planned to trap her. He attacks her with a knife, but Jennifer fights back and kills him in the tight space. She survives the long weekend, and when the doors open on Monday, she walks out shaken but alive. The final moment leaves you with the uneasy feeling that surviving one nightmare does not mean the danger is completely gone.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves tight, one-location thrillers.
